repo_classes.why: A 1,390,601-line initial commit and 0.99 vendored fraction were followed only by same-day style edits.
Three incremental commits build a custom data pipeline, chart frontend, replay mode, and support/resistance detector.
The repository identifies itself as a Stanford CS238 final-project submission and includes credited third-party LOB code.
A finished 19,756-line research artifact was deposited in one commit with no visible development history.
A Vite/shadcn-style frontend with extensive mock data sits atop a 0.99-vendored initial import.

exceptional.note: No original code repository has meaningful adoption: 1 total star and 0 forks received.

headline: An early-stage builder with one credible crypto-analysis project, alongside a public footprint dominated by course work and imported one-shot frontend artifacts.
evidence: `crypto-technical-analysis/server/data_service.py` separates symbol loading, CSV normalization, resampling, paginated Binance retrieval, and incremental-update helpers; `binance_api/download_history.py` implements a thread-safe weighted rate limiter.

`crypto-technical-analysis/support_resistance.py` defines domain-specific `SRParams`, `HorizontalZone`, `TrendLine`, `TrianglePattern`, and `ConsolidationZone` models rather than merely drawing API data.
`crypto-technical-analysis` shows an actual three-commit iteration over 2026-01-27 to 2026-01-30, including the explicit follow-up “plotting too many lines, logic needs to…” commit.

`CS238-RL-project` is explicitly labeled “Stanford CS238 Final Project”; `mc_model/environments/mc_lob_simulation_class.py` and `lob_utils/lob_functions.py` credit Hanna Hultin, so its sophisticated RL/LOB code cannot establish personal ML or systems depth.
The account has 34 public commits total, with activity in 2024–2026 but 0 commits before both the June 2021 Copilot and November 2022 ChatGPT cutoffs.
against: `consulting` was created and last pushed on 2025-09-09: its 1,390,601-line initial commit, 0.99 vendored fraction, and Figma-derived README do not demonstrate an engineering process.
`ff2` is a 680,703KB one-commit repository; its complete 19,756-line initial import provides no authorship or maintenance trail.
`crypto-technical-analysis` has only 3 commits over 3 days and reports no tests or CI; its FastAPI endpoints in `server/app.py` also duplicate validation and expose broad exception messages.
ask_for: A maintained, non-course original project with tests, CI, issue/bug-fix history, and a public commit trail would most raise confidence; a focused code sample showing the design and validation of the pattern detector would confirm the crypto-analysis specialization.
